title: A vapour of stars
caption: The dwarf galaxy DDO 82, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: DDO 82 · constellation Ursa Major · about 13 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble image shows DDO 82, also known as UGC 5692, a small galaxy that looks less like a grand spiral and more like a shapeless cloud of vapour. It lies about 13 million light-years away in Ursa Major, the Great Bear, and belongs to the M81 Group of around three dozen galaxies.

Few galaxies have the sweeping, glowing arms and bright centre of the Milky Way; most look more like DDO 82. Tiny as they are, such dwarf galaxies still hold anywhere from a few million to a few billion stars.

DDO 82 is not entirely formless. Astronomers class it as a Magellanic spiral, named after the Large Magellanic Cloud, a dwarf that orbits the Milky Way and is said to have a single spiral arm. In DDO 82, gravitational encounters over time seem to have scrambled that structure, so it is also described as a dwarf irregular galaxy.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.22 x 3.38 arcminutes) and distance (13 million light years), the frame spans roughly 12,000 × 13,000 light-years. Its light set out about 13 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys observed in visible and infrared light; the colour mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Part of this light is infrared and invisible to the eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Its name comes from its number in the catalogue of the David Dunlap Observatory, a list of dwarf galaxies compiled by the Canadian astronomer Sidney van den Bergh. The image combines visible and infrared exposures from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and covers about 3.3 by 3.3 arcminutes.
alt: A small, shapeless dwarf galaxy resembling a faint cloud of stars.
